title: La Bohème
note: 1.4.2: Pop-Up Video-style bubbles timed to the Met HD 2025-11-08 scene markers (982c4ee8-173a-53da-ae61-f575b27e9c42). Generated by facts/titles-snark/mk_title.py from spec_boheme.py.

facts.text: Today’s matinee is the Met’s 1,415th Bohème. The first was on 26 December 1900, with Nellie Melba as Mimì.
evidence: La Bohème (1415)
The Metropolitan Opera staged the work for the first time on 26 December 1900 with Nellie Melba as Mimì

facts.text: Host Matthew Polenzani knows this garret: the tenor has sung La Bohème at the Gran Teatre del Liceu.
evidence: "La Bohème" at Gran Teatre del Liceu

facts.text: Zeffirelli’s garret: a cutaway attic perched on the Paris rooftops, complete with tiles and smoking chimney pots.
facts.attribution: Thor Eckert Jr., The Christian Science Monitor, on this production’s Met premiere, 14 Dec 1981
evidence: The Bohemians' garret is a cutaway attic, quite literally set on the stage rooftops of Paris, complete with tiles, smoking chimney pots

facts.text: Our Marcello, Lucas Meachem, got his big break in 2006, discovered by Susan Graham at a karaoke bar. In Paris.
evidence: He had his big break soon after that in 2006, when he was discovered at a karaoke bar in Paris by acclaimed mezzo-soprano Susan Graham

facts.text: Bohème’s premiere, Turin, 1 February 1896, was conducted by a 28-year-old Arturo Toscanini.
evidence: The world premiere of La bohème was on 1 February 1896 at the Teatro Regio in Turin, conducted by the 28-year-old Arturo Toscanini.

facts.text: Juliana Grigoryan, our Mimì, won first and audience prizes at Operalia 2022. Her Met debut: Liù, in 2024.
evidence: the First and Audience prizes at the 2022 Operalia competition
She made her debut with the Metropolitan Opera in 2024 as Liù

facts.text: Puccini on this opera: “I lived that Bohème”, as a poor student, short of food, clothes and rent.
evidence: Puccini himself commented: "I lived that Bohème
he experienced poverty similar to that of the bohemians in La bohème, including a chronic shortage of necessities like food, clothing and money to pay rent

facts.text: “Che gelida manina” comes in three paragraphs: tender, then bolder at “Chi son? Sono un poeta”, then the love motif.
evidence: it has three distinct musical paragraphs
The initial part is tender, the second part (starting with Chi son? Sono un poeta) is distinctly different in tone, bolder
The third part starts with Talor dal mio forziere, the beginning of the 'love' motif used in the opera.

facts.text: Listen for the climactic high C on “speranza”: it’s unwritten, not in Puccini’s score.
evidence: the unwritten climactic high C (on speranza)

facts.text: Our Rodolfo, Freddie De Tommaso, entered London’s Royal Academy of Music as a baritone, then became a tenor.
evidence: studying at the Royal Academy of Music in London, where he entered in 2013 as a baritone and later changed to tenor

facts.text: As they realize they’re in love, the love motif from “Che gelida manina” returns.
evidence: the music returns to the opera's love leitmotif from Rodolfo's aria "Che gelida manina"

facts.text: The ending: Mimì’s high C, marked “fading away”, over descending harp harmonics. A major has become C major.
evidence: Mimì's last note is a high C, marked perdendosi (fading away)
The last bar in the orchestra is characterized by descending harp harmonics through the final C major chord
the key of A major, but ending in C major

facts.text: When this Act II set was unveiled in 1981, the audience roared for nearly a minute.
facts.attribution: Thor Eckert Jr., The Christian Science Monitor, on this production’s Met premiere, 14 Dec 1981
evidence: When the curtain rose on the second act
the audience erupted in a roar of acclaim, amazement, and even disbelief - a roar that went on for nearly a minute

facts.text: A stilt walker, a dancing bear, Musetta’s horse-drawn cab: “a Delacroix riot of reds and golds.”
facts.attribution: Charles Michener, Newsweek, 28 Dec 1981, on this production’s Met premiere
evidence: The carnival atmosphere of Act II, complete with a stilt walker, dancing bear and Musetta's horse-drawn hansom cab, is a Delacroix riot of reds and golds.

facts.text: Conductor Keri-Lynn Wilson made her Met debut in 2022–23. She also founded the Ukrainian Freedom Orchestra.
evidence: To commence her 2022/23 season, Wilson made her Metropolitan Opera debut
She is the founder and music director of the Ukrainian Freedom Orchestra.
Conductor Keri-Lynn Wilson

facts.text: Musetta’s Waltz is aimed at the people in the café as much as at us in the theater.
evidence: It is a song directed at the people in the café as much as at the audience in the theater.

facts.text: Heidi Stober began as a pianist and first planned to teach choral music. Then came opera.
evidence: She began her musical training as a pianist and initially was interested in pursuing a career as a choral music educator.
At Lawrence University she developed an interest in opera

facts.text: The act ends in a parade. At the 1981 premiere it brought some 240 people onto the Met stage.
facts.attribution: Thor Eckert Jr., The Christian Science Monitor, on this production’s Met premiere, 14 Dec 1981
evidence: which culminated in a huge parade, bringing some 240 people on the Met stage

facts.text: Watch the tavern door: a man in black rushes out, opens a black umbrella, and vanishes into the snow.
facts.attribution: Charles Michener, Newsweek, 28 Dec 1981, on this production’s Met premiere, calling it a “ghostly bit of stage business”
evidence: A man bundled up in black rushes out of the tavern
puts up a black umbrella and disappears into the wintry chill
this ghostly bit of stage business

facts.text: Two couples, two moods: Mimì and Rodolfo part tenderly while Marcello and Musetta quarrel fiercely.
evidence: Meanwhile, Marcello has found Musetta, and the couple quarrel fiercely about Musetta's flirtatiousness (quartet: Mimì, Rodolfo, Musetta, Marcello

facts.text: Check the sky behind the garret: silver-gray in Act I, rosy-peach now in Act IV.
facts.attribution: Charles Michener, Newsweek, 28 Dec 1981, on this production’s Met premiere
evidence: The vast, subtly changing sky behind the garret - silver-gray in Act I, rosy-peach in Act IV

facts.text: Zeffirelli turns Colline and Schaunard’s mock duel into a mad scamper along the rooftops.

facts.text: Jongmin Park bids farewell to Colline’s coat. He made his Covent Garden debut in this very role, in 2014.
evidence: He made his Royal Opera House debut in 2014 as Colline in La bohème

facts.text: Bohème closed the old Met house in April 1966. Zeffirelli then staged the new house’s very first production.
evidence: La bohème was the last opera performed at New York's Metropolitan Opera's original 1883 building on 16 April 1966
When the new Metropolitan Opera opened at Lincoln Center, he directed its first production
